pl-l4d30c2-d1e115.summary: Adds something about the mode of consent between Mary and Joseph.

pl-l4d30c2-d1e118.summary: Holds it may be believed that not only Mary but Joseph had resolved to keep virginity unless God commanded otherwise, and that they consented to conjugal society each understanding by the Spirit's revelation that the other wished to keep virginity; they had not expressed this in words, but later did, and remained virgins. Mary consented to marital society but not to carnal union unless God specially commanded it, by whose counsel she consented to the marital union, since she would not otherwise have consented, wishing to remain a virgin.
claims: Mary and Joseph both intended virginity.
Mary consented to carnal union only at God's command.

pl-l4d30c2-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine: blessed Mary resolved in her heart to keep the vow of virginity but did not express it in words; submitting to God's disposition, she consented to carnal union not desiring it but obeying the divine inspiration in both; afterward she and her husband expressed it, and both remained virgins.
claims: Mary entrusted her virginity to God and later both vowed it openly.

pl-l4d30c2-d1e131.summary: States, with Augustine, that their marriage was perfect, not in signification but in holiness, since marriages of those with a common vow of continence are holier.
claims: Their marriage was perfect in holiness.
Marriages with mutual continence are holier.

pl-l4d30c2-d1e137.summary: Quotes Augustine: what you both vowed to God by common consent you both should have kept; if he fell from that purpose, at least you persevere; he did not cease to be your husband because you both abstained, but you remained spouses all the more holily.
claims: Mutual abstinence does not dissolve marriage but sanctifies it.

pl-l4d30c2-d1e149.summary: Concludes that Mary and Joseph's marriage was perfect in holiness and also according to the threefold good of marriage: faith, offspring, and sacrament.
claims: Their marriage had all three goods.

pl-l4d30c2-d1e152.summary: Quotes Augustine: every good of marriage was fulfilled in Christ's parents: offspring, the Lord himself; faith, since no adultery; sacrament, since no divorce.
claims: Faith, offspring, and sacrament were fulfilled in Christ's parents.

pl-l4d30c2-d1e161.summary: Adds that only nuptial intercourse was absent, since in sinful flesh it could not occur without shameful concupiscence arising from sin, without which he willed to be conceived who was to be without sin.

pl-l4d30c2-d1e167.summary: Adds that though there was no conjugal intercourse, they were truly spouses in mind, not flesh, as also parents; though Ambrose says marriage is perfected by carnal union, the spiritual union being confirmed by bodily union, this means perfected as to signification, more perfectly figuring Christ and the Church, not as to the truth or holiness of marriage.
claims: Mary and Joseph were truly spouses.
Bodily union perfects marriage only as to signification.

pl-l4d30c2.summary: On the consent between Mary and Joseph: both had probably resolved to keep virginity unless God commanded otherwise, and consented to conjugal society, each understanding the other's intention through the Spirit; they later expressed and kept it. Mary consented to marital society and to carnal union only if God specially commanded it. Augustine: Mary resolved her vow in heart, entrusted her virginity to God, consented to carnal union not desiring it but obeying God, and later both expressed the vow and remained virgins. Their marriage was perfect in holiness, not in signification, and in the three goods, faith, offspring, and sacrament, lacking only intercourse, which could not occur without concupiscence. Ambrose's saying that bodily union perfects marriage concerns its signification of Christ and the Church, not its truth or holiness.
claims: Mary and Joseph both resolved to keep virginity unless God willed otherwise.
Mary consented to conjugal society, and to carnal union only at God's command.
Their marriage was perfect in holiness and in the three goods.
Bodily union perfects marriage only as to signification.
